{{Quote|Help me, Obi-Wan Kenobi, you're my only hope.''" [static] "''Help me, Obi-Wan Kenobi, you're my only hope.|Leia Organa's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
A '''hologram''' was a three-dimensional projection of a person or object, normally used in communication or entertainment.

==Operation==
{{Quote|Commander Cody, the time has come. Execute Order 66.|Commander Cody receiving a hologram from Darth Sidious|<ref name="Episode 3">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
[[File:YodaKashyyykHoloCouncil-ROTS.png|thumb|left|250px|[[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] participates in a holographic [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] meeting]]
Hologram technology was the basis for [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]'s most common form of communication.<ref name="EGWT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> Holograms were used mostly in telecommunications as an alternative to screens. A [[Holocamera/Legends|holocamera]] of any recorder or receiver would acquire the dimensions, form and movements of an object by means of ray scanning. This vision then could be transmitted simultaneously somewhere else, or stored and reproduced on a [[Holoprojector/Legends|holoprojector]] at a later time. Projected holographic images were visible from all sides, although matterless. Holograms were initially monochrome with a cyan hue, though following the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], an additional layer of color was added to some holograms. In full-duplex telecommunications, users could see each other's holograms, as if they were in the same room talking to each other, although not always in relative proportion.

Standard holograms had a lesser quality than screens, since they were mainly monochrome and often flickered. The luxury versions could produce incredibly lifelike full-color images, and were mainly used for entertainment purposes, such as at the [[Holographic Zoo of Extinct Animals]], or [[Hologram Fun World]], though they could also be used for disguises and other deceptions.

==Uses==
{{Quote|I can't watch any more.|Obi-Wan Kenobi upon seeing a hologram of Darth Vader slaughtering Jedi|<ref name="Episode 3" />}}
[[File:Shock.png|thumb|180px|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] watching a security hologram of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] kneeling before [[Palpatine/Legends|Emperor Palpatine]]]]
Portable [[Holovid/Legends|holovids]] could display a miniature hologram. Projectors were also implemented in many [[Starship/Legends|starship]] communication systems, for use by both pilots and passengers. Some [[Droid/Legends|droids]] (e.g., [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]]) could record and display holograms.

Members of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] could attend Council meetings via hologram if absent from [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] or otherwise unable to be there physically. Their image would project on their formal seat, and they would participate as if they were present.

[[File:Shield_must_be_deactivated.png|thumb|left|180px|Briefing hologram of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] and the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]] [[Prelude to Endor|before the]] [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]]]

Holograms were also frequently used in scientific projects as schematics. Likewise, they could be used in military operations and briefings. During the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], R2-D2 projected a hologram of the [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|Theed Royal Palace]] before organizing the assault. Prior to the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], a hologram of [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]] illustrated the attack plan to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]] pilots.

Holograms were also used in targeting practice. For instance, the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Army/Legends|army]] used holograms of [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]] and [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 super battle droids]], as well as holograms of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], to train their [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone]] [[Sniper/Legends|sharpshooters]] and improve their ability to distinguish between hostile and friendly targets.<ref name="Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Sharpshooter">{{SWArchive|url=games/playnow/sharpshooter|text=Sharpshooter|int=Sharpshooter (game)}}</ref>

Someone who forged holograms and passed them off as the real thing was known as a [[holo faker]].<ref name="POW">''[[Planet of Twilight]]''</ref>

Sentient programs would often use holograms as a method of interacting with living creatures. Sometimes, as in the case of [[Holiday (hologram)|Holiday]], the program would use holograms as their primary method of communication.

==Storage of holograms==
Holograms could be transmitted directly, or they could be stored in various storage devices (such as [[Hologram disc/Legends|holodiscs]])<ref name="Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]''</ref><ref name="Dark Forces: Rebel Agent">''[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent]]''</ref> and in [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech]] units or other types of droids. The storage device would be hooked up with a holoprojector in order for the stored image to be accessed. Many droids had built-in holoprojectors.

Hologram storage devices could be encrypted if their contents were deemed sensitive or classified. [[Morgan Katarn]] recorded and encrypted a hologram for his [[Kyle Katarn|son]] revealing his [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] heritage. The hologram was stored on a holodisc and could only be accessed by the [[Katarn family]] droid [[WeeGee]]. However, [[Jan Ors]] and [[Xiong Wong]] (with the help of [[Wires]]) managed to partially crack the hologram and display it, albeit in a very bad quality, to [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="Dark Forces: Rebel Agent" />
